gate_why: every postgame legendary is gated at the Champion (NETHER_DUNGEON_SCOPE.md section 8; Giratina, Darkrai, Necrozma, Mew). It also fixes the cap of everyone who may fight: after Blue the RCT cap is 100 (docs/mechanics/LEAGUE_LEVEL_CAP.md lines 20, 33, 56, 98: VERIFIED from rctmod source), so one level serves both phases.
level_why: the cap of whoever may fight it. The gate is champion_cleared and after the Champion the cap is 100; the level-cap catch block refuses a ball only STRICTLY above the thrower's cap (docs/research/notes/level-cap-catch-block.md line 116, 'over the cap is strictly greater'), so a level-100 Entei is catchable by every player this pack lets in. No alpha: Cobblemon's AlphaLevelMatchingSensor re-levels an alpha to the nearest player's highest level +4..+20 (docs/research/notes/legendary-species-1.8.0.md lines 99-112), which at 100 only clamps but is a trap the day the gate moves below the Champion. The balance (one level-100 legendary against six) is the open problem the scope names (section 4): trainer-balance-designer to tune, and EXP-059 X2 times a fight.

catch.rule: keyed on the CATCH, not the clear (docs/world-building/KYOGRE_CAVE.md:256-266, the scope's section 8). Until a player holds the advancement each run spawns their Entei with props.catch; it is granted by the pokemon_captured callback when that player catches an Entei while standing in their own slot, or in the slot their run held when it ended while they were offline (a relog catch of their run's left-standing Entei: review N142). From then on each run spawns props.farm (uncatchable). A catchable Entei that is fainted costs that run only.
catch.why_no_ball_check: the Hoopa cradle refuses other players' balls (tools/hoopa_cradle.py:233-247) because its Hoopas share one room. Here every run has its own slot and the keeper's sweep sends anyone who is not the slot's owner out within period_ticks (entei_boss/check), so nobody else can stand at the Entei to throw. The ball check is left out; if slots are ever shared it must come back.
catch.key_ball: a different check, about the BALL, not the player (the owner, 2026-10-08): bind adds data/key_ball.json `tag` to every Entei it binds, so only a Beast Ball (x5) catches it and any other ball, a Master Ball included, breaks free and is handed back (tools/key_ball.py). The claim still waits: a refused ball changes nothing in this pack, the Entei stays in battle, and a run that ends in a faint says 'It will be waiting when you return' as before. The farm-mode Entei carries the tag too; it is uncatchable, so the callbacks never see it.

theme: "The Tower After the Fire" (docs/mechanics/NETHER_ENCOUNTERS.md section 3.1; the re-theme owner-approved, relayed by the 2026-10-08 brief): a bell tower burned a hundred years ago, a ruin and a vigil, Entei the grief of the place and not its heat. Only the palette, the decor, the key's name and lore, the messages and the drop table carry it; the machinery (pocket slots, keeper, lockout, catch-once, blackout) is theme-neutral and unchanged. Superseded the same day: the first build's fire room (nether bricks, shroomlight, crying obsidian, the 'Ember Sigil', fire-themed drops), which NETHER_ENCOUNTERS.md section 0 P4 found was the fire room the brief rejected.

The first build's minecraft:blaze_powder was not: the record claimed 'no use of its own', but it is the brewing stand's fuel, a brewing ingredient, and an ingredient in 57 recipe or recipe-advancement files across the server's jars and the vanilla 1.21.1 jar (counted 2026-10-08 by this unit, read-only: eye of ender, fire charge, magma cream, Cobblemon's flame_orb, focus_band, focus_sash, expert_belt, rich_mulch, Mega Showdown's rotom_oven ...). A 1.21.1 recipe ingredient matches the item, not its components (ASSUMED, vanilla Ingredient semantics; not run), so the recipe book could fill an eye of ender with a sigil and a shift-click could put one in a brewing stand's fuel slot. No vanilla item has no use at all; minecraft:mourner_pottery_sherd (VERIFIED: assets/minecraft/models/item/mourner_pottery_sherd.json in the 1.21.1 jar) has one: the decorated pot's special recipe, four items laid out deliberately in a diamond. It is not on any bank buy list (tools/entei_boss.py problems; tools/economy_audit.py entei checks). It is not one of the recipe's ingredients. A mourner's sherd also suits a vigil; its icon is a clay fragment, not ash, which no 1.21.1 component can change without a resource pack (item_model is 1.21.2+)

recipe.why: MATERIALS, not money (the owner, 2026-10-10). The price is the economy design's: docs/mechanics/ECONOMY_OVERHAUL.md section 8 and build item U9 (integration branch, 213b1d8): 'Each entry consumes a key made from 2 netherite ingots', the same on every clear, in both modes, Challenge players included. No authored counter SELLS a netherite ingot: data/markets.json names it only as an exchange_for price (a line costing the bank value of N ingots), never as stock, so there is no cash path to a sigil (checked 2026-10-08; tests/test_entei_boss.py walks the stock lines). The bank buys netherite_ingot at 900 (data/bank.json:114), so a sigil destroys $1,800 of bank value (8 ancient debris and 8 gold): the run is a sink. key.refund: a sigil eaten where it cannot open anything (outside the Nether, during a run, before the Champion, inside the lockout, or with every slot busy) is given back at once with a line saying why: nothing is lost by eating it at the wrong time

entry.how: craft a Tower Ash anywhere; eat it anywhere in minecraft:the_nether. The consume_item advancement runs entei_boss/enter as the player, which checks the gate, the lockout, a free slot and that the player is in the Nether, stores where they stood, and teleports them into their slot in cobblers:pocket.
entry.why_not_a_placed_altar: a fixed Nether position needs Nether ground we cannot see: our heightmap is the overworld's, the rule forbids reading a world to decide a position (CLAUDE.md 'Ground comes from the heightmap'), the live world has never generated a Nether chunk, and the Nether structure override is being fixed tonight by another unit (docs/HANDOVER_SESSION.md section 3 item 1). A key used anywhere in the Nether needs no Nether ground (NETHER_DUNGEON_SCOPE.md section 2, recommendation).
entry.why_not_dialogue: tools/compile_dialogue.py's item check and take support count 1 from the main hand only (compile_dialogue.py:196-197, :227-228), and a dialogue needs an NPC standing at a position, which is the problem above. Crafting takes the materials atomically and needs no NPC.
entry.nether_check: dimension-safe without `execute if dimension`: `execute in minecraft:the_nether positioned as @s as @a[distance=..0.5]` finds the eater only if they stand in the Nether, because a positional player selector searches only the execution dimension (EXP-047 result 4). A bare @s selector is NOT dimension-checked by vanilla, so it is never used for this.

pocket.dimension_from: data/portals.json pocket.dimension: this pack does not define the dimension; cobblers_portals does, and it registers only at a server boot (EXP-047). tools/entei_boss.py fails closed if the two disagree.
pocket.slots_why: each player fights their own copy (the owner): one room per concurrent run. The group is a few friends (CLAUDE.md); a fifth simultaneous eater is refunded and told every room is kept
pocket.origin_why: z = -768 keeps every room outside the portals' rescue box (data/portals.json bands 0 and 256 with rescue_margin 512: z from -512 up), and every slot inside the shared world border (docs/STATE.md:74, playable x/z -1024..9215, one border for all dimensions in 1.21.1: docs/world-building/DIMENSIONS_AND_BORDERS.md:31-35) and outside the overworld map's bounds (data/world.json 0..8191), so no overworld checkpoint or waystone coordinate can coincide with a room (the blackout's waystone jump test compares coordinates, not dimensions). Slot k's centre is (origin.x + (k-1) * spacing, origin.z).
pocket.floor_y_why: the feet level, as data/portals.json pocket.floor_y: the generated bedrock plane is at y0

room.palette_why: NETHER_ENCOUNTERS.md section 3.1: charred-timber walls of stripped dark oak, a dark-oak log frame, a cracked-stone floor, daylight-coloured lamps (sea lanterns: the cold, wet light of the rain that put the fire out), the arch's sheet a pale grey. The section leaves the exact ids to world-content-dev: these are this unit's choice, every id VERIFIED in the 1.21.1 jar (assets/minecraft/models/item/<id>.json, read 2026-10-08), and the owner's in-game look (EXP-059 X3) is the judge. The walls are wood and a player's flint and steel can burn them; behind every one is the bedrock course, so a burned wall opens nothing

decor.why: the cracked bell, fallen and half sunk into the floor under the Entei's spot; set on the bedrock course, which carries a floor bell
the ring of cold ash where one of the three still will not leave (section 3.1): pale grey powder, resting on the bedrock course so it never falls

room.decor_why: every decor block is set INTO the floor course (y = floor_y - 1), never on it: the floor stays 17 x 17 standable less the arch's five (tests/test_entei_boss_audit.py walkable), the shell is unchanged, and tools/entei_boss.py problems() refuses a decor entry anywhere else. Not built, from section 3.1: the open roof and its rain (the room is a sealed shell, so the rain lives in the text) and the unlit campfire ring (a player can light a campfire, and a lit one burns whoever stands on it, as magma would: no_magma)
room.shape: a sealed box: interior 17 x 17, 10 high, from floor_y. One decorative course (floor, wall, ceiling), then a bedrock course outside it, so digging through the decoration meets bedrock; and the keeper gives the slot's owner Mining Fatigue IV while in the room (the gulch's ward, data/gulch_mine.json faces.why). Four lamps (palette.light) in the ceiling. The decor sits in the floor course around the Entei's spot. The exit arch stands against the low-z wall exactly as a portal room's (tools/portals.py room_blocks: arch at cz - half, its click one block in front, the arrival three in front). The Entei stands spot_dz south of the centre.
room.no_magma: no magma block and no campfire on or in the floor: either burns a player standing on it

keeper.arrive_delay_why: the Entei is spawned on the first keeper pass at least this long after the teleport, so the slot's chunk is loaded around the player before the spawn and its bind look for it
keeper.rules: every period_ticks, for each owned slot: is its owner standing in it? No -> the slot is freed (its Entei killed if loaded, its scores cleared, the owner's run ended if online). Yes -> the ward; any Entei carrying the slot's tag but not this run's number is killed (a stale one from a run that ended while its chunk was unloaded); the Entei is spawned once per run; a wandered Entei is put back on its spot. And every player in the band who is not the owner of the slot they stand in is sent out (entei_boss/eject).

lockout.why: one run per player per 24,000 ticks of game time (one Minecraft day, 20 minutes of server uptime), stamped when the sigil opens a slot. Counted from entry, not exit, so it needs no write to a player who logged out mid-run (a scoreboard cannot be changed for an offline player by selector). Game time stops while the server is stopped (ASSUMED vanilla, NETHER_DUNGEON_SCOPE.md section 1), so this is uptime, not wall-clock. Owner to tune; the sigil's materials are the other limiter.
lockout.score: eb.last, the game time of the player's last entry; carried across a re-export with data/scoreboard.dat (tools/carry_players.py:84)
lockout.never_entered: a player with no eb.last is outside the lockout whatever the clock reads: enter computes now - eb.last only when eb.last exists (a subtraction from a missing score would create it at 0 and refuse a never-entrant on a world younger than one lockout: review N142)
lockout.clock_reset: a re-export carries the scores but not level.dat's Time, so the game clock restarts lower than every carried eb.last. A negative now - eb.last is therefore outside the lockout (the run is allowed and re-stamps eb.last), never inside it; the cost is that a re-export ends every lockout early, once. The same for a slot's arrival stamp (eb.at): a negative delta restarts the arrival delay (review N142)

drops.entries_why: the tower's things (NETHER_ENCOUNTERS.md section 3.1): Charcoal, the timber; Smoke Ball, the smoke that never cleared; Damp Rock, the rain that put the fire out; Spell Tag, the unsettled; Cleanse Tag, the vigil kept; Life Orb, kept from the first table. The section's Sacred Ash is NOT in this pack: no item model or item definition named sacred_ash in any jar under the server's mods/ (searched 2026-10-08, read-only), so Cleanse Tag stands in its place. Weights flat, as the section says. Superseded the same day: Fire Gem x2 (4), Heat Rock (3), Red Mint Seeds (3), Flame Orb (2), Magmarizer (2), Life Orb (1), the first build's fire-themed table
drops.rule: ONE roll per farm-mode run, for the slot's owner, when their uncatchable Entei faints in a battle (the battle_fainted callback, tools/gulch_mine.py:1670-1691's pattern, matched by species and by the player standing in their own slot instead of by UUID: the slot holds one Entei and one player). Given straight into the owner's inventory with `loot give`, the portals pedestal's command (tools/portals.py claim). Items, never money.
drops.item_ids_verified: every id exists as assets/cobblemon/models/item/<id>.json in Cobblemon-fabric-1.8.0+1.21.1.jar under the server's mods/ (read-only with zipfile, 2026-10-08, for the re-themed table; the research note's evidence for item ids)
drops.not_bankable: tools/entei_boss.py fails closed if any drop is on the CobbleDollars bank's buy list (modpack/config/cobbledollars/bank.json, which carries the base list plus data/bank.json buys): PP Up and PP Max were dropped for that reason (the base bank buys them at 2,500 and 3,500). It also refuses any *_plate id (no Arceus plates, the owner) and any CobbleDollars item.
drops.why_these: battle items that are the tower's things (entries_why), each with no route of its own or a single shop line (Charcoal is a counter's type booster: data/bank.json exchanges.floors.held_item); a flat table, no scaling with repetition (NETHER_DUNGEON_SCOPE.md section 3). WEIGHTS AND ITEMS ARE A PLACEHOLDER for trainer-balance-designer: the scope's collection table (no repeats until complete) is option A work.

loss.rule: losing to the Entei blacks the player out like any wild loss (the owner): the blackout's battle_loss_wild charges the flat $600 and sends them to their checkpoint in the overworld, healed (tools/blackout_pack.py:222-235, :291-300, :358). The Entei carries the blackout's claims.exempt_tag (data/blackout.json:71, read at generation), so it makes NO item claim and never becomes a guardian: a guardian in a pocket slot that is freed the moment its victim leaves would hold their items in a room nobody can return to.
loss.after: the player is out of the slot, so the keeper's next pass frees it and kills that Entei. The sigil is spent; the lockout runs from entry.
loss.flee: running from the battle ends the battle, not the run: the Entei stays on its spot and can be fought again until the player leaves by the arch
loss.death_outside_battle: a death in the room (the Entei attacking outside a battle, if Fight or Flight makes it hostile) goes through the blackout's death path; the player respawns in the overworld and the slot is freed. Whether a legendary is aggressive here is EXP-059 X4

objectives_why: per player: eb.id (own number from #next, the arena's ar.id pattern), eb.slot (the slot of their current run, 0 none), eb.last (game time of last entry), eb.clears (catches plus farm defeats), eb.runs (entries), eb.rx/ry/rz (the Nether block they ate the sigil in, y rounded up). Per slot, on fake players #s1..#sN: eb.own (owner's eb.id, 0 free), eb.run (this run's number, also stamped on its Entei), eb.mode (1 catch, 2 farm), eb.sp (spawned), eb.roll (the run's reward settled), eb.at (entry time). eb.t is scratch.
fallback_out: data/blackout.json pallet.position, in the overworld: where eject sends a player whose return point was never stored

message.enter: The ash is cold on your tongue. Rain, and a tower long after the fire.
message.appear: Something rises from the ash ring. It has been waiting.
message.refund_dimension: The tower remembers only the Nether. You keep the ash.
message.refund_run: The tower already holds you. You keep the ash.
message.refund_gate: The tower does not know you yet. The League's Champion has to fall first. You keep the ash.
message.refund_lockout: The vigil is not over. Try again in about this many minutes:
message.refund_busy: Every room of the tower is kept by someone else. You keep the ash.
message.caught: Entei goes into the ball. It does not have to wait here any more.
message.faint_catch: Entei sinks back into the ash ring. It will be waiting when you return.
message.drop: Something of the tower's is left in the ash.

message_why: NETHER_ENCOUNTERS.md section 3.1: appear and out are the section's own lines; the rest are this unit's in the same voice (aftermath: wet, grey, quiet; the grief of the place, not its heat). The colours stay the generator's (tools/entei_boss.py say)
does_not_cover: two players fighting ONE Entei together: each player fights their own copy (the owner), and a shared wild battle is NETHER_DUNGEON_SCOPE.md X5, which needs a second account
an Entei fainted outside a battle (by a sword or a Pokemon not in a battle) gives no drop: only battle_fainted rolls. The gulch's slain path (tools/gulch_mine.py:1599-1610) is not reused

a player who logs out mid-run: their slot is freed on the next pass; when they log back in they are sent back to where they ate the sigil on the next pass. Their sigil is spent and their lockout runs. Their run's Entei, if its chunk unloaded first, is loaded again by their return and killed by the keeper's free-slot sweep on that same pass; a ball thrown before it counts as their catch (slot/s<k>/relog_caught grants the flag: review N142), so it is never a second catch

an Entei whose chunk unloaded before its slot was freed stays frozen until that chunk next loads, when the keeper kills it: the free-slot sweep if the slot is still free, the run-number check if it is owned again
anything about Heatran or a rotation: option A
the Nether's own generated content (Moltres altars, Blaine copies): another unit, tonight
